question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**agreeable**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The passage talks about a sense of freedom while being alone in a carriage.
 
• The word should suggest that the form of liberty is one that can be enjoyed or is pleasant in its simplicity.
 
• "**Agreeable**" means pleasant or enjoyable, aligning with the description of liberty.
 
• Other options ("**detestable**", "**humour**", "**miserable**") do not fit the context of describing an enjoyable or pleasant form of liberty.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *There is a pleasant__ sense of freedom about being alone in a carriage that is jolting noisily through the night. It is liberty unrestrained in a very **__agreeable__** form. You can do anything you like. You can talk to (3) ______ as loud as you please and no one will hear you. You can have that argument out with Jones and roll him triumphantly in the dust (4) ________ fear of a counterstroke. You can stand on your head and no one will see you. You can sing or dance a two-step or practise a golf stroke, (5) ______ play marbles on the floor without let or hindrance.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Detestable **(घिनौना): "Detestable" means deserving intense dislike, which contradicts the sense of freedom being discussed.
 
• **Humour **(मज़ाक): "Humour" means the quality of being amusing, which does not convey the intended idea of freedom in form.
 
• **Miserable **(दुखी): "Miserable" means very unhappy or uncomfortable, which is the opposite of the pleasant sense of freedom mentioned.
